children: The war in the Middle East will continue to dictate energy prices and financial markets as major central banks have hiked rates to combat inflation, while calls to slow AI advancement could impact the sector that has supported global stocks, credit issuance, and commodities.
These matters, in addition to trade, are expected to lead focal points in the highly anticipated meeting between US and Chinese Presidents Trump and Xi.
US economic data releases will be headlined by durable goods orders.
The US will also join the Eurozone aggregate and major economies, Japan, Australia, and India in PMI results.
In turn, Australia will release its labor data, and India is set to publish infrastructure output.
Lastly, central bank decisions are awaited in China, Switzerland, Sweden, Norway, Mexico, and Indonesia.

title: Week Ahead - Sep 21st
